items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: was that a Saturday Night Live skit where they were doing the Mr. Rogers take-off with the bass player?

ctx.x: So you’re not in a position, I mean around here the union wasn’t involved in any of that, so you wouldn’t be in that kind of position where the guy paying the bill might think, well, you weren’t here very long.

You just played a note, but then you also, you have to get there. I mean the majority of the time for doing a local session you have to get there, you have to be warmed up, you have to be ready to play anything, and that’s what they’re paying you for. They’re not © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

paying you for your note, you know. What was the old — was that a Saturday Night Live skit where they were doing the Mr. Rogers take-off with the bass player? And he’s going yeah, I’m just thinking about how much I get paid for notes. No, it doesn’t work like that. You know, they’re paying you for your expertise and whatever you’re doing, you’re playing whatever part they need.
